In the FEED phase the sizing, properties, etc. of some equipment can be optimized to provide a better fit for the respective application. As far as practicable we have included American equipment manufacturers and suppliers in our lists of potential equipment suppliers. The following sections describe the main equipment types required as part of this development and some representative suppliers. Final selection of equipment types including material selection will be carried out in FEED. Page53 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 4.3.1 CO₂ COMPRESSION The plant consists of two liquefaction trains, each with three stages of compression. Given the plant duty, centrifugal compressors have been considered as they offer the best all round solution, with two options being: 1. In-line Compressors:  Generally more expensive option  Highly reliable  Good access and maintainability  Reduced ability to optimize speeds due to each stage driven from the same shaft 2. Integrally Geared Compressors:  Typically cheaper than in-line  Less reliable  Each stage can be optimized due to running on its own pinion  Sensitive to vibrational issues, especially with variable speed drives  Prone to surge i.e. each stage could require an anti-surge valve Typical Integrally Geared and In-Line Compressor skids are shown below. As part of the next FEED phase, evaluation of the two options should be part of the equipment technical solution review. The compressors shall be designed, manufactured, and tested in accordance with API 617. Typical compressor suppliers used by Entr are:  Siemens  Mitsubishi Heavy Industries  MAN-Turbo  Elliott Turbo  Baker Hughes Page54 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version Figure 4.3: Siemens In-Line Compressor Skid Figure 4.4: MAN Integrally Geared Compressor Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) use on compressors provides significant benefits like reduced energy consumption, improved system efficiency, minimized motor inrush current during startup, better pressure control, extended component lifespan, and overall operational cost savings by matching production to actual demand.
